summary: The LLM landscape in 2026 is dominated by a handful of frontier families from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with strong open-weight competition from Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen. Enterprise adoption is increasingly mediated through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, which substantially amplify real-world usage beyond direct-API numbers. Because several newer named models in the research data (e.g., GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4) cannot be reliably confirmed as currently available with stable naming, this ranking focuses on models with verifiable availability and documented adoption.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Highest API call volume of any model and widely available through Azure OpenAI and other aggregators, making it the default choice for most enterprise and developer workloads.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications and multimodal assistants

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: The go-to model for coding and agentic workflows, with heavy adoption via Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Anthropic's direct API.
models.best_for: Software development and complex agentic automation

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Dominant in enterprises on Google Vertex AI with a very large context window, driving strong adoption across Google Cloud customers.
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and multimodal enterprise tasks

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Extremely popular for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads thanks to very low pricing and large context, widely consumed through Vertex AI.
models.best_for: High-throughput, latency- and cost-sensitive production workloads

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B MoE reasoning specialist with massive HuggingFace download volume and extremely low pricing, making it the leading open reasoning model for developers.
models.best_for: Cost-effective reasoning and math/coding tasks on self-hosted or API infrastructure

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: The most downloaded open-weight general model on HuggingFace and widely offered on AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, making it a default for self-hosted and private deployments.
models.best_for: Self-hosted and privacy-sensitive deployments requiring customization

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: A high-performance open MoE model delivering near-frontier quality at a fraction of the cost, driving rapid developer adoption for general-purpose tasks.

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's flagship reasoning model, heavily used for complex problem solving and available via the OpenAI API and Azure, with growing enterprise adoption.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, research, and high-stakes analytical tasks

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading model with strong enterprise adoption, available on Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI, favored for data-sovereignty-conscious deployments.
models.best_for: European enterprise and multilingual applications with compliance needs

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: A top-performing open MoE model with surging HuggingFace downloads, especially strong in multilingual and coding tasks and widely adopted in Asia.
models.best_for: Multilingual and self-hosted deployments, particularly in Asian markets

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost model with strong adoption for high-volume tasks via Bedrock and Vertex AI, clustering closely with the top 10 in enterprise usage.
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive tasks needing Claude-quality output at lower cost
